OCR_Text: यथा दृष्टि तथा सृष्टि।
Translation: As is the sight, so is the creation.
Explanation: How a person looks at the world determines how the world appears to them. External reality mirrors a person's inner vision or perspective.
Keywords: Perspective, Perception, Drishti, Drishti Srishti, Reality, Consciousness

OCR_Text: वैं २३ सप्तमी च दिवाकरः कालमुद्गतं च न खङ्गैतं सामुद्रचं निर्मलं रैं २३ सीरोढं शामलं हारमञ्च रैवतं योवरे रुडमणिं च यादियं ज्ञेउं प्लेकट् कानिच रैं २४ अर्धचेंतं तया सुभं केसरं सर्वं गहूर्षु २५ रो विमलो ततः रैं वेयकं मुत्तमेन २५ अंगुलीयक रत्नानि समस्ताः स्वगुलीयके च विश्वकर्मोद्भवं चैव परमे च अतिनिर्मलं रैं २६
Translation: And the seventh is the sun, having risen in time, and not struck by swords. The oceanic, immaculate, plough-borne, dark, necklace-resting, Raivata, the ruby of the youth, and the aquatic should be known as the Plekato. And the half-moon, then auspicious, all the filament, desirous of seizing, and pure; then the necklace with best pearls, all the finger-rings upon one's own ring, that which originates from Viśvakarman, and supreme, exceedingly immaculate.
Explanation: The passage lists various items and elements, including the sun risen on time and untouched by swords, specific gems and ornaments like the oceanic, plough-borne, dark, Raivata, and aquatic ones known as the Plekato, a half-moon, filaments, and best pearls. It concludes by mentioning finger-rings containing all gems, as well as an exceedingly pure and supreme object created by Viśvakarman.
Keywords: Gemology, Ratna, Precious stones, Navaratna, Jewelry translation, Sanskrit manuscript

OCR_Text: भी० स० १ श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥ जनमेजय उवाच ॥ शरत ्ने शयानस्तु भारत नो पितामहः । कथमुस्सृजवादे हंकं वियोगमधारयत् ॥ १ ॥ वैशंपायन उवाच ॥ शृणु बाप हितो राजन्नुसुचिर्भूत्वा समाहितः । भीष्मसुकु रुशाईल देहोत्सर्गसमाश्रयत् २ निवर्धमानेखय नेऽत्तरे वैदिवाकरे समाविशघरात्मानमात्मन्येव समाहितः ३ शुक्लपक्षस्य चष्टम्यां माघमासस्यपा शिव १
Translation: Salutation to the deities. Obeisance to Lord Ganesha.   Janamejaya said: O descendant of Bharata, while resting upon the bed of arrows, how did our grandfather abandon his body and endure that separation?  Vaishampayana said: Listen, O king, for your own welfare. Being purified and deeply focused, hear how Bhishma, the tiger among the Kurus, resorted to the casting off of his body. While the sun was moving in its northern course (Uttarayana) and entering [the northern hemisphere], with his mind completely concentrated upon the supreme Self within himself, on the eighth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Magha...
Explanation: King Janamejaya asks how his grandfather Bhishma abandoned his body and endured separation while resting on a bed of arrows. Vaishampayana tells the king to listen with a pure and focused mind as he describes how Bhishma cast off his body. This event occurred on the eighth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Magha, while the sun was moving in its northern course and Bhishma's mind was completely concentrated on the supreme Self within himself.
Keywords: Janamejaya, Vaishampayana, Bhishma, Sharatalpa, Uttarayana, Dehotsarga

OCR_Text: सुद्योविष्णुः पराद्धर्त्तस्सर्वाश्चैवैतु देवताः परिगृह्य
Translation: Visnu, shining brightly, having encompassed the ultimate half and all the deities, proceeds forth.
Explanation: Brightly shining Vishnu moves forward after gathering all the deities and the ultimate half.
Keywords: Visnu, shining brightly, ultimate half, deities, proceeds forth, Sudyovisnu

OCR_Text: बृहस्पतेष्ट्वा साम्ना ज्येनात्रिंचाम्मसा विति म म्य य स्लातित द्बृहस्पते रेवेनमेत सा युज्धं ससो कुतांगमयति ।२४। अथाहा स्म्राड् युम ्सो सम्राड् युमस्ता वितिनिवदित मे वेनमेत संताद्वेण्यो निोदय थेयं महा वीर्यो यो न्य ५३ बेची येयुंमुष्पाए के को मृतं गो पायते ये खेत ५१ दाह त्रिष्ट्च आहतित्रर दियङ्गः ।२५। अयो जितीः जुहोति वा वाचयति वाय दि जुहोति यदिवा च यति समानु एवं धुः ।१६। स वा वाचयति अनि रैकाक्षरैए प्राए मुदजयत मुज्ेषं प्रजापतिः सप्तदशा क्षरेए सप्तदश षः स्ताम मुदजयत मज्जेषमितितद्युदेवताभिरेतादेवता उड्द
Translation: By the Sāman of Bṛhaspati, by the waters, [you are purified]—thus he unites him. Thereby he unites him indeed with the [Sāman] of Bṛhaspati, and leads him to the heavenly world. Then he says, "You are the sovereign ruler, the shining one; you are the sovereign ruler, the shining one"—thereby he establishes him securely in the sovereign realm. This one is of great heroism, who has... protects the immortal. Therefore he recites the Triṣṭubh verse, for Vena is... Then he offers the *jitī* (victory) oblations, or causes them to be recited; whether he offers them or causes them to be recited, the result is just the same. He causes them to be recited: "With the monosyllable, Agni conquered the out-breath; Prajāpati conquered that victory. With the seventeen-syllabled [metre], the seventeenth stoma conquered; [Prajāpati] conquered that victory"—thus [he recites], through these very deities, raising up those very deities.
Explanation: A priest unites a person using the Sāman of Bṛhaspati and water to lead him to the heavenly world, and then proclaims him as a sovereign ruler to firmly establish him in that realm. He recites a Triṣṭubh verse for Vena and performs or has someone recite the *jitī* victory oblations, which yields the same result either way. Finally, the recitation tells how Agni and the seventeenth stoma conquered victory through specific syllables and meters.
Keywords: Bṛhaspati, Sāman, Samrāṭ, Triṣṭubh, Jitī oblations, Prāṇa

OCR_Text: सर्वं कारणोद्भवमस्ति ।
Translation: Everything arises from a cause.
Explanation: Every object and event in existence comes into being because of a cause. Nothing happens without a preceding cause.
Keywords: Pratītyasamutpāda, Causality, Hetu, Cause and effect, Origination, Sarva

OCR_Text: श्रीः कृ०आ० हृ० ७५२ बृहन्मित्रस्यवरुणस्यशर्मापस्यामुरुवीराअरिष्ठाः ॥ तिस्रोभूमीमीधिरयंत्रीरुतद्यूंत्रीणिब्रताविद्येअंतरेष्याः । ऋतेनादित्यामहि वोमहिब्लंतदर्यमन्वरुणमित्रचाह ॥ त्रीरोचनादिव्याधारयंतहिरण्ययाःशुचयोधासपूताः । असञ्जतोअनिमिषा अदब्धाउरुशंसाऋतज्ञवेमर्त्याय ॥ त्वंविश्वेषामरुणसिराजाथेचेदेवा असुरयेचमर्ताः । क्षान्नौरास्वणारदोविचसेषणामायूंषिधत्तानिप्पूर्वा ॥ नदक्षिणमिविचिकेतेनसव्यानप्राचीनमादित्यानोनतृप्स्थाः । याक्पाविदसचोधीर्याविछुष्यमानीतोअभयंन्योतिरेषाः ॥ योराजञ्चक्र्तनिनभोदद्यांयवर्धयंतियुष्ठयक्ष्यग्नित्याः । सरेवान्यातिप्रथमोश्धेनवसुधोवाविधेयंशुप्रप्रास्तः ॥ सुचिरपःसुयवसाभद्रउपसेतिवृइवयाः सुवीरः । नकिष्टुंब्रंपंतितोनदूराघआदित्यानांभवतिप्रणीतौ ॥
Translation: May we find the broad, heroic, and inviolable shelter of the great Mitra and Varuna. Three are the earths supporting this, and three are the heavenly realms holding the ordinances, to be known within the realms. By the cosmic order (Ṛta), O Ādityas, great is your mighty power—this do Aryaman, Varuna, and Mitra declare.  Three radiant, heavenly lights they hold, golden, pure, and consecrated by the ritual. Unconquered, unblinking, and unimpaired, of wide praise and knowing the Ṛta, they watch over the mortal.   You, O Varuna, are the king of all, of those who are gods and those who are mortals. Grant us, O protectors, long-lasting lives, filling our days.  Neithering the right nor the left, nor the ancient do the Ādityas satiate. Whatever sins are committed, may you dispel them, and grant us fearlessness and light.  O King, who measures out the sky and expands the heaven, whom the warriors invoke with sacrificial fire—he truly moves as the foremost possessor of wealth, bestowing treasures, brilliant and far-reaching.  Good are the waters, good the pastures, auspicious is the approach for one who is rich in horses and heroes. No one diminishes them, nor are they far distant when guided by the protection of the Ādityas.
Explanation: The passage is a prayer to the deities Mitra, Varuna, Aryaman, and the Ādityas asking for their safe shelter, long lives, protection from sin, and the removal of fear. It describes these divine figures as kings and watchers over mortals who hold up the earth and heavens, maintain cosmic order, and bestow wealth, water, and good pastures.
Keywords: Mitra-Varuna, Ādityas, Ṛta, Cosmic Order, Vedic Hymn, Divine Shelter

OCR_Text: ततः स विस्मयाविष्टो हृष्टरोमा धनञ्जयः । प्रणम्य शिरसा देवं कृताञ्जलििरभाषत ॥ १४ ॥
Translation: Filled with wonder and with his hair standing on end, Dhananjaya, bowing his head before the divine Lord and joining his palms in reverence, spoke thus.
Explanation: Filled with wonder and excitement, Dhananjaya bowed his head and joined his palms in reverence before the divine Lord. Following this, he spoke.
Keywords: Dhananjaya, Vismaya, Anjali, Bhakti, Arjuna, Divyadrishti

OCR_Text: मऽम्प्णाय चावस्व-न्याय च नमो नादेयाय च दीप्चाय च ३१ नमो ज्येष्ठाय च कनिष्ठाय चनमः पूर्वजाय चापरजाय च नमो मध्यमाय चापगल्भाय च नमो जघन्याय च बुब्भयाय च नमः सोम्बाय ॥ ३२ ॥ नमः सोम्बाय च प्रतिशर्त्याय च नमो याम्याय च क्षमप्राय च नमः श्लोक्या य चावसान्याय च नम ऊर्ध्याय च षल्र्याय च नमो वन्द्याय ॥ ३३ ॥ नमो वन्द्याय च कक्ष्या य च नमः श्रवाय च प्रतिश्रवाय च नमः आशुषेणाय चाशु रथाय च नमः शूरया च निनि- दने च नमो विस्मिन ॥ ३४ ॥ नमो विल्मिने च कवचिने च नमो वार्मिणे च वरूथिने च नमः श्रुता- य च श्रुतसेनाय च नमो दुन्दुभ्याय चानन्याय च नमो धृषवे ॥ ३५ ॥ नमो धृषवे च प्रप्र- शाय च नमो निषङ्गिणे विषुङ्गिते च नमस्तीक्ष्णेषवे चायुधिने च नमः स्वायुधाय च सुध- न्वने च ३६ ॥ नमः सुत्याय ॥ नमः सुत्याय च पथ्याय च नमः काट्याय च नीप्याय च नमः
Translation: Salutation to the protector of the rivers and to the illuminated one; salutation to the elder and to the younger; salutation to the first-born and to the later-born; salutation to the middle one and to the inexperienced one; salutation to the lowest one and to the bubbhya (one who moves in bubbles/water); salutation to the one accompanied by Uma.  Salutation to the one accompanied by Uma and to the one dwelling against the current; salutation to the southern one and to the patient one; salutation to the renowned one and to the final one; salutation to the elevated one and to the broad one; salutation to the venerable one.  Salutation to the venerable one and to the one in the forest/secret place; salutation to the hearing and to the echo; salutation to the swift-army and to the swift-chariot; salutation to the valiant one and to the fault-finder; salutation to the astonishing one.  Salutation to the helmeted one and to the armored one; salutation to the mail-clad one and to the defender; salutation to the renowned one and to the leader of a renowned army; salutation to the maker of the kettle-drum and to the incomparable one; salutation to the bold one.  Salutation to the bold one and to the pre-eminent one; salutation to the quiver-bearer and to the one with arrows pointing both ways; salutation to the one with sharp arrows and to the armed one; salutation to the well-armed one and to the owner of a good bow; salutation to the soma-presser.  Salutation to the soma-presser and to the traveler on the path; salutation to the one of the thorny thickets and to the one of the waters/rivers; salutation.
Explanation: The passage offers repeated bows or salutations to various forms, qualities, and roles of a divine figure. It honors opposites and pairs, such as the elder and younger, the first-born and later-born, the swift-armed and the chariot-rider, as well as those equipped with armor, helmets, quivers, and sharp arrows.
Keywords: Shatarudriya, Rudra, Yajurveda, Namaskara, Vedic litanies, Epithets of Shiva

OCR_Text: सं. १ श्रीडुंढिराजाय नमः ॥ श्रीगणपतिभ्यो नमः ॥ ॐ॥ अग्निमीळे पुरोहितं यज्ञस्य देवमृत्विजं । होता रं रत्नधाततमं॥ अग्निः पूर्वेभिऋषिभिरिळ्यो नूतनैरुत । स देवाँ एह वक्षति॥ अग्निर्नायिमश्नवत्पोषमेव दिवे दिवे । यशसं वीरवत्तमं॥ अग्ने यं यज्ञमध्वरं विश्वतः परिभूरसि । स इदेवेषु गच्छति॥ अग्नि होता कविक्रतुः सत्यश्चित्रश्रवस्तमः । देवो देवेभिरागमत्॥ यदंग दाशुषेत्वमग्नेभद्रं करिष्यसि । तवेत्तत्सत्यं गिरः॥ उप त्वाग्ने दिवे दिवे दोषावस्तर्धिया वयं । नमो भरंतमसिराजंतमध्वराणां गोपांऋतस्य दीदिविं वर्धमानंस्वे दमे॥ सः पितेव सुनवेऽग्ने सूपायनो भव सचस्वा नः स्वस्तये॥ वायवायाहि दर्शतेमेसोमाअलंकृताः। तेषांपा हि श्रुधीहवं ॥
Translation: Salutation to Lord Dundhiraja! Salutation to Lord Ganapati! Om!  I praise Agni, the domestic priest of the sacrifice, the divine minister, the hotar, the best bestower of wealth.  Agni, who is to be praised by ancient sages and by modern ones as well, may He bring the gods hither.  Through Agni, one obtains wealth, daily nourishment, and fame accompanied by heroic offspring.  O Agni, whatever sacrificial ritual you encompass on all sides, that indeed reaches the gods.  Agni is the hotar, possessing the wisdom of a sage, truthful, possessing most wondrous renown; may the god come with the gods.  Whatever blessing, O Agni, you will bestow upon the pious worshipper, that truth belongs to you alone, O Angiras.  Unto you, O Agni, day by day, O guardian of the night, we bring our prayers, paying homage—to you who rule over the dark, the protector of sacrifices, the shining guardian of cosmic order, growing in your own abode.  O Agni, be easily accessible to us like a father to his son; abide with us for our well-being.  O Vayu, come hither, O handsome one; these Soma-juices have been prepared. Drink of them and listen to our call.
Explanation: The text begins with salutations to Lord Dundhiraja, Lord Ganapati, and Om, followed by praises to the fire god Agni as a priest, minister, and bestower of wealth. It describes Agni as being praised by past and present sages, bringing the gods to the ritual, and carrying sacrifices and prayers to them. Worshippers ask Agni for daily nourishment, fame, blessings, and fatherly protection, while also inviting the handsome god Vayu to drink the prepared Soma-juice and listen to their call.
Keywords: Rigveda, Agni, Vayu, Hotar, Soma, Vedic hymn

OCR_Text: श्रीः अः १ ॥श्रीगणेशायनमः॥ श्रीपुरुषोत्तमाय नमः॥ श्रीकीर्तनाद्रे वनप्रयेनियम्यसंसारजगतः॥ उमादिभिषजेभेजरामसूरूर स्तमः ॥ १॥ रगादि रोगान्तानामुत्पन्नान्येषकायप्रस्तानानेषा न तत्सकामोहतरनिदान्ञ्ञानयोर्पर्ववैद्याय नमोम्स्तमसे ॥ ग्रथाननप्राग्रकामियस्मथायेंव्याख्यास्यामः इत्यनत्सलाइगगेया ग्रामतत्पयेः आयुष्कामायमानेनथर्माथंसर्वसाधनम् आयुर््वे शेषदेशेषविधेयःपरमादरः ब्रह्मासरत्तायुषोवेद्रेप्रजापतिः मजिन्नरान्मोष्थिनौतोमस्त्रसांतमोत्रिउडसिकास्थनीन् ने गिनवैशादिकांस्तेचथयच्रेवाणितेनिरे तभ्फतिविप्रकीयोभ्यः प्रायःसारनरोस्मयः क्रियतेशेगरुदयेनानिसेतिप्रविस्तरत्म् कायबालग्रदोर्धांगशल्यदंष्ट्राजगराधान ग्रच्छावेर्गानितस्याइ चिकित्सानोपमेस्थिता वायुःपित्तकफभेतित्रयोदोषाःसमासतः॥ रामः
Translation: Salutation to Sri. Salutation to Sri Ganesha. Salutation to Sri Purushottama. Salutation to Sri Kirtanadri. May He who, through the forest-like path of worldly existence, binds and cures the ailments of the universe along with Uma and others, the dispeller of darkness, the supreme physician for the afflictions beginning with passion and other diseases—to that Supreme Light, I offer my prostrations.  Now we shall expound upon this treatise, fulfilling the foremost desires [of the seekers]. As stated: "For one desiring longevity, righteousness, wealth, and the means to all accomplishments, utmost regard should be bestowed upon the science of life (Ayurveda) in every way."   Brahma remembered the Veda of longevity and imparted it to Prajapati. Prajapati taught the Ashvini twins, and they instructed Dhanvantari. Dhanvantari taught Bharadvaja and others, and they composed various treatises. For the benefit of those whose intellects are feeble, this essence is gathered here, avoiding unnecessary prolixity.  The eight branches of this [science] are: internal medicine (Kayachikitsa), pediatrics (Balachikitsa), psychiatry (Graharoga), treatment of diseases of the upper body/ENT (Urdhvanga), surgery (Shalyatantra), toxicology (Danshtratantra/Agadatantra), geriatrics (Jaratantra/Rasayana), and aphrodisiacs (Vajikaranatantra).   In brief, the three humors (doshas) are Vata, Pitta, and Kapha.
Explanation: The text begins with prostrations to the Supreme Light, who cures the ailments and worldly existence of the universe. It then introduces a treatise on Ayurveda, stating that the science of life should be studied for longevity, righteousness, wealth, and accomplishments, tracing its lineage from Brahma down to various sages. Finally, it outlines the eight branches of this medical science and lists the three bodily humors as Vata, Pitta, and Kapha.
Keywords: Ayurveda, Kayachikitsa, Tridosha, Dhanvantari, Ashtanga, Shalyatantra

OCR_Text: विकृताविकृतादेहैर्जेज्ञ्ज्ञिते वर्त्तयेति चे । तेषामिपेपिराज्याभ्यो र्ष्टोमथोधे संश्रयः ॥ वयोहेशरात्रिभुक्तानां तेष्वनतमथादिगः। क्रू। मातृ तैर्भवेदिष्ट्मग्नि तो ग मन्दअग्निः समैः समः कोरूः क्रूरारूः इमेशोमथस्थाःन्नैः समैरपि सुक्ताभवस्र्जैन्मादौ विषेलो ववि घक्रिमेः तैम्नतिःः प्रकृतयो हीनमथोग्न्यमः एथक समधात समस्तास्तथेशानियाहितोषष्ठा तगङ्गलालतुः शीतःनरः सृत्स मलोनिलः पित्रेम्मुसेरती तो गमेलन्तुविषेस्ररेंश्वम् स्निग्धः शोणो गुरु मेदः स्थूलो रुक्तः स्थिरः कफः मेसर्गमीत्रिधातृञ्च तद्धृत्रितयकोपततः रसास्त्वमांसमेदोध्विमज्जाशुक्राणिधातव सप्रहव्यामलामुत्राशुक्रत्तेदारयोपि च वृद्धिसमानैः सर्वेषां विपरीतैर्विपर्थ्ययः रसाः स्वादुप्रलवणतिक्तोषष्णकषायकाः षड्द्रमाश्च्रितास्तैस्तत्त्वयाथैवं बन्लवयदाः तत्रयामारुतंज्ञेति

Explanation: The passage describes the physical origins, humors, and tissues of the body, noting that the body's condition depends on its elements and food intake. OCR_Text: ॥ आद्य ॥ २ ॥ प्रायःलिङ्गादयः कफं कषायत्रक्रमधुपित्तमयेनुरुर्वते श मनेकोपन्नेनस्वचरितेदव्यमितिप्रथिता उष्णशीतगुणोत्कषीनां अवीर्येद्विधास्मृतम् त्रिधाविपाकेद्रव्यमस्खा अम्लकटुकात्मकाः गुरुमृदृहिंगाभिषायतथार्तणसारइरउस्थिराः शुणास्मत्त्वसृवि घराविशतिनिह्मविपर्ययः कालावथकर्मणांयोगादीनमिर्ष्ये त्रिमात्रकाः सम्यगेगस्सवितेयोगेरोगपरोरैषेककारणाम् रोगसन्देहवैषव्यसंरोगसाम्यमरोगता निजगतंत्रविभागेननतः अरोगाद्विधामताः तेषांकायमनोभेदैः रढिष्ठानमपिद्विधा रजस्तममृतमसोहैौश्यरोगास्तुयाहयतो दर्शनस्पर्शिनप्रश्नैः।१ परीक्षेतवरोगिणाम् रोगेननिधानं प्रागपलक्षणोपशयांसि भिः श्रमिश्रदप्रभेरेनरेगशमाङ्गहिरधिया ज्ञानात्वेवानिभून् यस्मावूपंत्कफाल्वनं साधारणसममलेत्रिधाभृदेशमारी
Translation: Generally, signs and symptoms associated with Kapha, mediated by astringent and sweet tastes, along with Pitta, are pacified by specific therapeutic substances and regimens. Virya (potency) is traditionally recognized as twofold due to the predominance of hot and cold attributes, while Dravya (substances) undergo a threefold Vipaka (post-digestive effect)—namely, sweet, sour, and pungent. Heavy, soft, oily, unctuous, stable, and firm properties constitute the physical qualities, whereas their alterations lead to various disorders. Diseases arise from the improper or excessive combination of time, intellect, and action (Karma).   Through the threefold measure of proper application, under-application, or excessive application, illness or health ensues. Doubt regarding disease, its severity, balance, or complete eradication (health) is understood through the systematic division of endogenous and exogenous disorders, which are broadly classified into two categories. Their locus of manifestation is also twofold, classified by body and mind. Rajas and Tamas represent the mental coverings associated with diseases.   A physician should examine patients through observation (darshana), palpation/touch (sparsha), and interrogation (प्रश्न/prashna). The diagnosis of a disease is established by understanding its etiology (nidana), prodromal symptoms (praag-upakshana), actual symptoms, and therapeutic tests (upashaya). By means of careful differentiation, mixed symptoms, and clear intellect, a wise physician eradicates disease at its root. Thus, based on the three fundamental humors (doshas)—vata, pitta, and kapha—in their balanced, aggravated, or diminished states, the manifestations of bodily conditions are ascertained.
Explanation: Kapha and Pitta symptoms are pacified by specific treatments and substances, while the potency of substances is twofold (hot and cold) and their post-digestive effect is threefold (sweet, sour, and pungent). Diseases are caused by the improper or excessive combination of time, intellect, and action, resulting in either illness or health based on proper, under, or excessive application. A physician examines patients through observation, touch, and questioning to diagnose and eradicate diseases by understanding their causes, symptoms, and bodily humors.
Keywords: Virya, Vipaka, Tridosha, Rogapariksha, Dravya, Chikitsa

OCR_Text: ज्योतिष १११ ॥श्री गणेशाय नमः ॥हरिः ओ३म् ॥ पंचवत्सरमयं युगाध्यक्षं प्रजापतिं। दिनत्वयनमासांगं प्रणम्य शिरसा शुचिः ॥१॥ प्रणम्य शिरसा कालं विद्याय सरसं वती ॥ कालज्ञानं प्रवक्ष्यामिल्गधस्य महात्मनः ॥२॥ ज्यो निषामयनकस्तत्रं प्रवक्ष्यांभ्यनुपूर्वशः ॥ विप्रार्णसमतं लोके यतका लार्थ सिद्धये ॥३॥ निरेकं द्वादशाब्दं द्विगुणं गत संज्ञिकं ॥ षष्ट्याष ष्ट्या युतं काभ्यां पर्वणो राशि रुच्यते ॥४॥ स्वराऽर्क मेके सोमा कैर्य दासा के सवा सवो ॥ स्यात्तदा हि युतं माद्य स्तपः शुक़ो दिनं त्यजः ॥५॥ १ प्रपद्ये ॥११॥
Translation: Jyotisha  Salutations to Lord Ganesha. Om. Bowing my head in purity to the Lord of progeny, the creator, who embodies the five-year cycle (Yuga), and whose limbs are the days, solstices, and months; having bowed my head to Time and to the eloquent goddess of learning (Sarasvati), I shall set forth the knowledge of time for the great-souled Lagadha. I shall explain the astronomical science (Jyotisha) in due order, as approved by the Brahmins in the world, for the achievement of temporal goals. A period of twelve years, devoid of remainder, when doubled, is termed "gat" (elapsed); combined with sixty and sixty by means of these, the zodiacal sign (rashi) of the conjunction (parvan) is known. When the sun and moon are in the same constellation... [passage continues with technical calculations of lunar-solar positions]. I take refuge.
Explanation: The author begins by offering respectful salutations to Lord Ganesha, the creator, Time, and the goddess of learning, Sarasvati. Following this, the author states an intention to explain the science of astronomy (Jyotisha) and the knowledge of time for Lagadha, as approved by the Brahmins. Finally, the text introduces specific time cycles and calculations involving a twelve-year period, zodiacal signs, and the positions of the sun and moon.
Keywords: Vedanga Jyotisha, Lagadha, ancient astronomy, Kala-jnana, lunar-solar cycles, astronomical science

OCR_Text: रु २ तेश्रविष्ठादौ सूर्याचंद्रमसाबूदकः॥ सर्पार्धेदक्षिणार्क्कस्तुमाघः श्रावणे रा १ योः सदा॥ई॥धर्मरहरिरांप्रस्थः क्षपौ सौदगता तो॥ दक्षिणेतो विपर्य स्तो षमुहूर्त्ययनेनतु॥७॥ द्विगुणंसप्तमं वाऊरयनाद्यंत्रयोदश॥ चतु र्धंदशमंचैव द्वियुग्माद्यंबऊले व्यतो॥ वसुस्त्वष्टाभगोजश्च मि त्रसर्पाश्चिनोजलं॥ धाताक श्राद्यायना श्रा ऊ पंचैन भ... स्खतु ना डी॥ भांशास्युरषकाः कार्याः पक्षाद्वादशवो कृताः॥ एकादशगुणस्योनः भु क्लैर्दैव इवायदि॥१०॥२॥ कार्याभांशाषका स्थाने कुलाये काल विंशतिः॥
Translation: Beginning with Śraviṣṭhā, the sun and the moon are watery. When half of serpents (Āśleṣā) is reached, the sun turns southward; Māgha is in [the month of] Śrāvaṇa, and [the path] of the rays is constant.   Day and night are like Indra's threshold; nights are northerly, and days are southerly. In the southern [path], it is the reverse, with respect to the fifteen-muhūrta [equinox] by means of the ayana. The bhāṁśa-ṣaṣṭhīs should be made as ṛṣakas, and the twelve fortnights are made. Less than eleven times is the bright [fortnight] as if divine...   One should perform the bhāṁśa-ṣaṣṭhī in its place, [which is] twenty [parts] of time in the family [tradition].
Explanation: The sun and the moon are watery starting from Śraviṣṭhā, and the sun turns southward when reaching the middle of Āśleṣā. Keywords: Śraviṣṭhā, Ayana, Muhūrta, Nāḍī, Bhāṁśa-ṣaṣṭhī, Nakṣatra

OCR_Text: कलाण्यधिशुकं तथा॥८॥ कुमराश्चषयानश्व तथा नक्षत्तारवारिअः। ततो नक्षत्र- शिखिनोऽष्ट तथैव वारिजं तथा॥९॥ नक्षत्रातवारिजै जातमेतरिवाक्रमात्॥ षट्चंद्रशङ्खानांच क्रमो यं परिकीर्तितः॥११॥ अथ शराद्यपरज्ञानमाह॥१३॥ द्वि-वेद-गन-मधोऽधु त्रयस्य चैकमेकैकमेकम्-विषम्-विभागेन चाधुकृशं॥ चेदेका राय- तितथोर्ध्वगा वरे स्वातत्स्याधोगगनमध्ये पुनस्तथैव॥ १२॥ त्रैलोक्यं चक्रदारवी जंभ- स्टाकं क्षुद्रवारिजं॥ तद्वै गदितं स्पष्टं शक्रज्रमलेषु च॥ १३॥ रेरेखाणां नयातिच क्रमेण प्र- क्रमेण प्रकिंतं ध्यायनवरे रेजै मान संज्ञं॥ व्यस्तांत ह्यादितरी रेखा यये नातोर्ध्व ऋ नये छैछै- जक्रमधो ततश्च शून्यं॥ १४॥ करहग्धिपरिरीटगणनस्याद्यदि रेखे खतुमध्धगोप्यह- ह्ढिं॥ गगनेऽवकवासिथंतदास्माद्दिपरीतेऽतुमा- रये लाग्निधा॥१५॥ अथ धोरेयाहद्धे- तदुपरिननश्रोपरिग तोध्वज जोलो नाये हुर्रमसवरे श्रेपि कुमरा॥ नाये ह्यस्ता- सास्पाच्छलज विधि विशेषं अमुननेष- याज्ञा रप्पो ज्ञेयो विमलतरम- जेशा कुजगते॥१६॥ शून्यध्वयैस्पाद्यदि चोर्ध्वं सोरिस्रितंततत्स्तुरे खाछ यके क्रमेण॥ तथाच शून्य त्रयमहा- संष्टि तरे रेवेक द्वास्या त्त्तदधश्च तिर्य गा॥१७॥ नक्षत्तारवारिज संज्ञ के नाये चंद्रतव- रारिजसं ज्ञ के दे तथान्यतः॥ व्यस्तांत द्रवति यदा रिवाजम्निधंसदिज्ञेयंसमयमिदं
Translation: Then follows the *adhiśuka*, and likewise the *kum̄ras*, *ṣaṣayāna*, and the water-born *nakshatra*. Then eight *nakshatra-śikhins*, and likewise the water-born. From the water-born *nakshatras*, this is produced in due order. This is declared to be the sequence of the six moons and conches. If there are two zeros, and upward it is thus inclined, then upon the line in proper order. And thus the great combination of three zeros, another single line being below it, and transversely.   Under the designation of the *nakshatra-vārija*, and likewise another under the designation of the lunar water-born. When it flows inversely as the *rivāja*, this indeed is to be known at the proper time as the destruction.
Explanation: The passage lists various elements in sequence, including the *adhíśuka*, *kum̄ras*, *ṣaṣayāna*, water-born *nakshatras*, eight *nakshatra-śikhins*, moons, and conches, and describes specific measurements, lines, and numerical divisions. It then details the placement and arrangement of lines, zeros, and symbols relating to the hand, eye, body, and sky, along with upward and reverse movements. OCR_Text: नः समाधिमाभावयति क्लेशांश्चप्रतन्मकरोति प्रतन्मकृतक्लेशांन् प्रसंख्यानाग्निनादग्धबीजभावस्तानप्रसवधर्मिणः करिष्यति ते षांस्तनूकरणात्पुनः क्लेशैर्खरारामृष्टासत्पुरुषान्यमतामात्रख्या तिः सूक्ष्मप्रज्ञासमाप्ताधिकांराः प्रतिप्रसववायकरिष्यंति तेषां तनूकरणात्पुनः क्लेशैः अयपुनः क्लेशः कियंतोवेति अशिया सेत्रमुतरेषांप्रसुवृत्तनुविच्छिनोदाराणां ४ अत्रअविद्यासे त्रप्रसवभूमिरुत्तरेषां अस्मितादीनांचतुविकाल्पानांप्रसुवृत नुविच्छिनोदाराणां तत्रकामसुतिः चेतसित्रक्तिमात्रप्रतिष्ठा नाबीजभावोपगमः तत्तप्रबोधओलेबनेसंमुखीभावः
Translation: It brings about deep meditative absorption (samadhi) and weakens the mental afflictions (kleshas). Having thus weakened the kleshas, it burns their seed-nature with the fire of discriminative discernment (prasamkhyana), rendering them incapable of sprouting again. Through this attenuation, the kleshas—no longer touching the self like unbaked clay—culminate in a subtle state of direct insight, which is the sole realization of the distinction between the pure consciousness and the mind. Once their function is fulfilled, they merge back into their primal source (pratiprasava).   Regarding this, one might ask: what and how numerous are these kleshas? Here, the answer is given: the field and birthplace for ignorance (avidya) and the subsequent [afflictions—asmita, raga, dvesha, and abhinivesha]—which manifest in four states: dormant (prasupta), attenuated (tanu), intercepted (vicchinna), and fully active (udara).   Among these, the dormancy of desire consists of the mind remaining anchored merely in the potentiality of attachment without active expression. Its awakening is its direct manifestation when stimulated by its object.
Explanation: This text explains that meditation weakens mental afflictions and burns their seeds through discriminative discernment so they cannot grow back. These afflictions exist in four states—dormant, attenuated, intercepted, and fully active—with ignorance serving as their birthplace and field. Furthermore, desire remains dormant when the mind holds only the potential for attachment, and it awakens when stimulated by an object.
Keywords: Samadhi, Kleshas, Prasamkhyana, Pratiprasava, Avidya

Translation: Om. Salutations to Lord Ganesha. Now begins the second pada.   How does the yoga of a person whose mind is unified relate to one whose mind is distracted? To explain this, Kriya Yoga is introduced: austerities (tapas), recitation of sacred texts (svadhyaya), and devotion to the Lord (ishvara-pranidhana) constitute Kriya Yoga. Translation: By those means also one should accomplish the stability of the mind. Or else, a sensory-oriented activity (vishayavati pravrittir) arising in the mind binds it to stability. When one concentrates upon the tip of the nose, there arises the experience and perception of divine fragrance; at the tip of the tongue, the experience of divine taste; at the palate, the perception of form; in the middle of the tongue, the experience of divine touch; and at the root of the tongue, the perception of divine sound. These generated activities bind the mind to stability, dispel doubt, and become the gateways to meditative wisdom (samadhi-prajna). By this same principle, it is to be understood that activities arising in regard to the moon, sun, planets, jewels, lamps, and rays of light are likewise sensory-oriented (vishayavati). Even though the truth—as comprehended through scripture, inference, and the instruction of a preceptor—becomes fully illuminated by wisdom, possessing the capacity to establish reality accurately, yet so long as even a single aspect is not directly perceived by one's own internal instruments (antahkarana), all of it remains as if indirect (paroksha) and fails to generate a firm conviction regarding subtle matters such as liberation and the like. Therefore, for the purpose of subduing [doubt and indirectness] alongside scripture, inference, and the preceptor's instruction...
Explanation: The mind's stability can be achieved by focusing on sensory activities, such as concentrating on the tip of the nose to experience divine fragrance, or on different parts of the tongue and palate to perceive divine taste, form, touch, and sound. These experiences stabilize the mind, remove doubt, and lead to meditative wisdom, similar to focusing on the sun, moon, jewels, or lights. However, even when truth is taught by scriptures, logic, and teachers, it remains somewhat indirect until at least one aspect is directly experienced by one's own internal senses to firmly establish conviction in subtle matters like liberation.
Keywords: Manasa Sthiti, Vishayavati Pravritti, Samadhi Prajna, Divya Gandha Samvid, Antahkarana Samvedya

And when the mind attains absorption in the sense of ego (asmitā), it becomes like a boundless ocean without waves, peaceful, infinite, and consisting solely of "I-am-ness." Regarding this, it has been said: "Realizing the self as consisting solely of that measure, 'I am.'"
Explanation: Investigating a specific meaning helps the mind grasp even the subtlest subjects related to liberation, which is the purpose of mental purification that leads to unobstructed faith, energy, mindfulness, and concentration. Additionally, focusing the mind on the heart produces a sorrowless and luminous state where the intellect's nature shines like celestial bodies. Finally, when the mind absorbs into the ego, it becomes a peaceful, infinite, and wave-free ocean consisting solely of "I-am-ness."
Keywords: चित्तपरिकर्म, mental purification, विशोका ज्योतिष्मती, sorrowless luminous meditation, अस्मिता, asmitā ego-sense

OCR_Text: अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रं पश्यामि त्वां सर्वतोऽनन्तरूपम् । नान्तं न मध्यं न पुनस्त्ववादिं पश्यामि विश्वेश्वर विश्वरूप ॥ १६ ॥
Translation: I see You everywhere with infinite forms, possessing countless arms, stomachs, mouths, and eyes. O Lord of the Universe, O Cosmic Form, I see neither Your end, nor Your middle, nor Your beginning.
Explanation: The speaker sees the Lord everywhere in infinite forms with countless arms, stomachs, mouths, and eyes. The speaker also states that the Lord has no visible beginning, middle, or end.
Keywords: Vishvarupa, Cosmic Form, Infinite Vision, Ishvara, Divine Form, Universal Lord

OCR_Text: न तृणादिष्वखिलावकालो भेषजयोऽगकृत् । शोधने शमने चेति समासायोषधं द्विधा ॥ शरीरज्ञानायोधाएं क्रमेणापरमीक्षथम् । संस्विरेको वमने तथा तैलेच्छूने मधुः धीवैर्यात्तथाशि विप्तानमनोरोषोधेषपम् भिषद्रद्याएवस्यातारो वीणादा । चतत्रयं चिकित्सितस्थानिरिहेंप्रतेकेचंअत्रंगेणम् दत्तनौ यां तृणशास्त्राथो तत्सकमां सुविभिषक, वइर्कालयउद्हूयणेसः । मात्रयोगप्रमोघथम् अत्ररक्तसुविदेत्तोमतिमान्यारिवाकरै ग्राप्तोरोभीषवशेषपातापकास्मात्वानापे सर्वौषधत्तमे । रेदेशनः पुंसोनितात्मनः अ्रमममगोल्यदेतद्यइपइपोऽनुपद वः मृतलघ्घरोघन्तप्रतिपारसेपरि गृहेषनुगलेयेकदो । घमागोडामृतः शस्त्रादिसाधनः क्रुकुसैकरेखततोगदः शेषनारायेवायाळः पथ्याभ्यासाहिपयंगे अत्रणक्रसप्पवः
Translation: Medicine, which cures ailments, is not found among mere grass and the like. In summary, medicine is twofold: purificatory (shodhana) and pacifying (shamana). For the comprehension of the body, these two methods are to be examined in order: oleation, induced vomiting, and honey for swelling, sustained by patience and a steady mind. Physicians who understand the fourfold branches of therapeutics are truly accomplished here. The wise physician, knowing the appropriate dosage and time, extracts the root of disease like a skillful boatman steering across water. The supreme medicine is that which cures the disease completely without causing further harm, aided by proper diet and conduct.
Explanation: Medicine is divided into two types: purificatory and pacifying. To understand the body, one must examine methods such as oleation, induced vomiting, honey for swelling, and maintain patience and a steady mind. A wise physician uses the correct dosage and time to remove the root of a disease, while the supreme medicine cures the illness completely without causing new harm with the help of proper diet and conduct.
Keywords: Medicine, Shodhana, Shamana, Therapeutics, Dosage, Diet

OCR_Text: पश्यामि देवांस्तव देव देहे सर्वांस्तथा भूतविशेषसंघान् । ब्रह्माणमीशं कमलासनस्थमृषींश्च सर्वानुरगांश्च दिव्यान् ॥ १५ ॥
Translation: O Lord, within your body I see all the gods, as well as the diverse hosts of beings—Lord Brahma seated upon the lotus, all the seers, and the divine serpents.
Explanation: The speaker looks inside the body of the Lord and sees all the gods, different groups of living beings, and Lord Brahma sitting on a lotus. Also visible inside the body are all the seers and the divine serpents.
Keywords: Visvarupa, cosmic vision, divine form, Brahma, seers, serpents

Translation: Salutation to Sri Rama! Salutation to that holy Guru, who is of the nature of the syllable Om, faultless, formless, all-pervading, and present in all moving and unmoving beings; salutation also to the Supreme Guru.
Explanation: This passage begins with a greeting to Sri Rama. It then offers salutations to the holy Guru, describing him as formless, faultless, all-pervading, existing in all moving and unmoving beings, and having the nature of the syllable Om. Finally, it offers a salutation to the Supreme Guru.

OCR_Text: तत्रैकस्थं जगत्कृत्स्नं प्रविभक्तमनेकधा । अपश्यद्देवदेवस्य शरीरे पाण्डवस्तदा ॥ १३ ॥
Translation: There, at that time, the son of Pandu beheld the entire universe, divided in many ways, yet standing as one in the body of the god of gods.
Explanation: At that time, Arjuna, the son of Pandu, looked upon the body of the supreme god. Within that divine body, he saw the entire universe existing together as one, even though it was divided in many different ways.
